correctness.rationale: The exact KKT scaling and positive root determine the unique optimizer for every m,n>=2; nonnegative four-block hard limit exists precisely when p+q<=1. Blockwise L1 differences give TV=2x. Monotonicity in pq and p+q proves the global worst case, with exact rationalized Hall-slack formula and boundary layer. The complete log-column Jacobian has gauge eigenvalue 1 and exactly one nontrivial eigenvalue lambda=(x-pq)^2/[p(1-p)q(1-q)]; two elementary AM–GM inequalities bound it sharply with equality at balanced Hall marginals. Standalone finite checks: 8467 passed, including independent differentiation of the Sinkhorn map; proof, not finite checks, establishes universal scope.

value.rationale: Replacing forbidden edges with finite large-M costs is a motivated optimization practice. The exact dimension-free penalty budget quantifies mass leakage while preserving both marginals; the Hall-boundary crossover distinguishes square-root from linear exponential leakage; and the coincident slowest local Sinkhorn factor quantifies a concrete conditioning cost of stronger masking. These are natural sharp tradeoffs on a complete, non-arbitrarily-chosen one-edge model, beyond correctness or a routine sample computation. No claim of practical algorithm acceleration or general sparse-mask theory is made.
